react_result.final_narrative_text: The three complementary pathway-analysis paradigms converge on tyrosine metabolism as the dominant affected pathway. RaMP multi-DB ORA ranked KEGG:map00350 Tyrosine metabolism first with an FDR of 2.98e-09 and fold-enrichment of 626.6, with four input metabolites — norepinephrine, pyrocatechol (mapped to catechol), L-tyrosine, and homocysteine — hitting a 69-member pathway. Mummichog m/z-direct activity ranked the same pathway #1 (p=7.56e-04) on the KEGG human_mfn network, capturing L-tyrosine, tetrahydrobiopterin, norepinephrine, and ornithine. MetaboAnalystR KEGG PSEA confirmed KEGG:hsa00350 (the human-curated equivalent of the same pathway) as top hit (p=0.0065) with norepinephrine and L-tyrosine. This three-tool consensus is reinforced by two secondary signals: biopterin metabolism (Mummichog rank 2, p=0.0063) implicating tetrahydrobiopterin as a cofactor in tyrosine hydroxylation, and the urea cycle/amino-group metabolism (Mummichog rank 3, p=0.0063) linking ornithine to nitrogen handling. The biological story is a coordinated disruption of the tyrosine degradation and catecholamine biosynthesis axis: L-tyrosine sits at the entry point, feeding both the catecholamine branch (via tyrosine hydroxylase, requiring tetrahydrobiopterin as cofactor) toward norepinephrine, and the aromatic catabolic branch through homogentisic acid and pyrocatechol. Homocysteine contributes via the transsulfuration pathway, whose overlap with tyrosine metabolism is well-documented. No structural conflicts were identified among the resolved metabolites — the two homocysteine InChIKey variants share the same block14 (FFFHZYDWPBMWHY), confirming they are charge-state tautomers of the same compound.

L-Tyrosine (KEGG:C00082) is the entry-point substrate; it is metabolised through two branches — the catecholamine biosynthesis arm via tyrosine hydroxylase (requiring tetrahydrobiopterin as cofactor) toward norepinephrine (KEGG:C00547), and the aromatic catabolic arm through homogentisic acid (KEGG:C00544) and pyrocatechol (KEGG:C15571).

L-Tyrosine (KEGG:C00082) is the entry-point substrate; it is metabolised through two branches — the catecholamine biosynthesis arm via tyrosine hydroxylase (requiring tetrahydrobiopterin as cofactor) toward norepinephrine (KEGG:C00547), and the aromatic catabolic arm through homogentisic acid (KEGG:C00544) and pyrocatechol (KEGG:C15571).
